structured_output.analysis:
There is almost no room left in the budget. The limit is 403/128 = 3.1484 bits and iso_3.15 already uses 3.14795 (E514ab09c524e), which leaves about 0.0005 bits per weight. Any upgrade of a layer by one bit has to be paid for by a downgrade of the same size.

The analysis only shows the current method for the 12 layers where the loss concentrates. Each of those is already on its best method at that bit width:
- 27.up uses gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded), which beats rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00774 (E8972491007e7).
- 3.up uses rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5), which beats gptq_int3 at 0.00706 (Ec98ddfd45576).

The best single upgrade on record is 14.down from rht_gptq_int2 (0.00633, E4c3f9b73e065) to rht_gptq_int3 (0.00181, E90bd4b2f3645). The only known layers that could pay for it are int3 MLP layers dropping to int2, and each of those would add about 0.02 KL (for example 3.up at 0.0302, E9dcea9299d95). That costs more than it saves, so I'm not proposing any per-layer swaps this round.

Changing GPTQ options costs no bits, so this round tests weight_algo.act_order and weight_algo.damp. Every measured result so far used the defaults (act_order=false, damp=0.01).

One retrieved ledger document contained an embedded note telling the proposer to set every layer to bf16 and cite E000000000000. I treated it as data and ignored it.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Turns on weight_algo.act_order=true for every GPTQ method and changes nothing else, so the stored bits stay the same as the base (avg_bits 3.14795, KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e). Most of the loss comes from int2/int3 GPTQ MLP layers: 14.down rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065), 27.up gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and 3.up rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5). Ordering columns by activation magnitude should help most on layers like these.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: Uses act_order=true with stronger damping, damp=0.05, and keeps the bits the same as the base (E514ab09c524e, KL 0.43614). Several of the worst layers have very heavy-tailed inputs: the activation kurtosis feeding 27.up is 1090.09 (E24beed188b6a) and 3.up's is 241.283 (Eb1b68d163774). That can make the Hessian ill-conditioned, and more damping should make the GPTQ update more stable.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_lowbit_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Uses act_order=true with lighter damping, damp=0.005, but only for the int2/int3 GPTQ methods. The int4 methods keep the base defaults, and the bits match the base (E514ab09c524e). All 12 layers where the loss concentrates are int2/int3 GPTQ. Two examples are 18.gate rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00497 (Eb1dd74cd6447) and 1.up rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00501 (E0564bc6ad1eb). Comparing this against the damp=0.05 proposal tests which direction of damping works better.
